name: Plant Anatomy & Physiology

objectives.text: Identify the roots, stem, leaves, and flower of a plant
Describe how the roots, stems, leaves, and flowers each help a plant live and grow
Compare taproot and fibrous root systems in common crops and garden plants
Explain how plants respond to light, gravity, water, and touch through tropisms
Diagram the parts of a leaf, including the blade, petiole, and veins, and explain the function of each part
Identify the parts of a flower, including sepals, petals, stamens, and pistil, and explain the role of each in plant reproduction
Identify the structures of a typical plant cell, such as the cell wall, central vacuole, and chloroplasts, and explain the function of each
Explain how xylem and phloem transport water, minerals, and sugars through a plant
Explain the function of plant cell organelles and how specialized cells form dermal, ground, vascular, and meristematic tissues
Identify the components, types, and functions of plant roots, including the root cap, root hairs, and modified storage roots in crops such as carrots and sweet potatoes
Identify the components and functions of plant stems, including nodes, internodes, buds, and modified stems such as tubers, rhizomes, and stolons
Describe leaf morphological features such as arrangement, venation, and margin and explain how they relate to overall plant growth
Compare the arrangement of vascular tissue in monocot and dicot stems and roots
Analyze how guard cells and stomata regulate gas exchange and water loss through transpiration
Evaluate the function of xylem, phloem, and cambium tissues and their impact on plant systems, such as the effects of girdling or trunk injury on a tree
Analyze primary and secondary plant growth, including the roles of apical and lateral meristems and the formation of annual rings
Analyze plant responses to growth regulators such as auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins, ethylene, and abscisic acid and their role in tropisms and crop production
Explain the stages of plant growth and the methods and reasons for controlling growth through practices such as pinching, pruning, and applying growth retardants
Evaluate how flower structure, including perfect and imperfect flowers and monoecious and dioecious plants, affects plant breeding, production, and use
Recommend management strategies for a greenhouse, field, or SAE crop that apply knowledge of transpiration, translocation, and assimilation
Evaluate how a plant's vascular and structural adaptations suit it to its native environment
Design an agriscience investigation suitable for an SAE or FFA Agriscience Fair that tests how an environmental factor affects a physiological process such as transpiration rate

changes: Kept and lightly reworded all six original objectives because each names a real competency. Added a grade 3 functions step and elementary objectives on root systems, tropisms, flower parts, and plant cells. Added grade 9 to 12 objectives aligned to AFNR Plant Systems standards on cell organelles and tissues, roots, stems, leaf morphology, monocot and dicot vascular arrangement, cambium function, secondary growth, growth regulators, growth control, and flower structure in breeding. Also added a transpiration and translocation management recommendation and an SAE or FFA agriscience investigation. Photosynthesis, germination, propagation, and identification content was left to the sibling sub-topics.
